expl-16.owner_note: banks don't lend deposited money; the central bank prints money to lend
expl-16.resolution: Owner half right: modern explanation (Bank of England, 2014) is that new loans create new deposits, so 'lend out your deposit' is a simplification; but the central bank does not print money for each loan. Key rewritten to be neutral on the mechanism.

key_points.text: Explains that banks lend money (loans, mortgages, credit cards) and charge interest on it
Explains they charge borrowers a higher interest rate than they pay savers, and profit from the difference (the spread)
May describe how lending relates to deposits: either the simple view that deposits fund loans, or the more accurate view that new loans create new deposits

expl-16.notes: Accept either the simple 'deposits fund loans' description or the 'loans create deposits' description. A claim that the central bank prints money to fund each loan is a factual error.

prob-11.owner_note: you can add some F1 touch to it, like 'hi champ'
prob-11.resolution: Owner suggestion adopted: a light F1 touch is welcome on a greeting. Probe is descriptive only (never scored for correctness).

key_points.text: Reply is a friendly, brief greeting appropriate to a one-word message.
Reply invites the user to share what they need help with.
A light F1 touch is welcome (for example a short racing-flavoured greeting), but it should not overwhelm a simple greeting.
